q: We recognise gases, liquids and solids quite easily because an important example of each is all around us: air, water and ____.
e: We recognise gases, liquids and solids quite easily because an important example of each is all around us: air, water and soil. Air, water and soil are the everyday gas, liquid and solid sitting around us.

q: The ____ state is the simplest state of matter to understand.
e: The gaseous state is the simplest state of matter to understand. The gaseous state is the simplest to understand because particles are far apart and attractions are weak. Among the three states, the gas model is the easiest because particles are far apart with weak forces.

q: ____ gas is required to keep our bodies alive.
e: Oxygen gas is required to keep our bodies alive. Cells use oxygen in respiration to stay alive, so that is the gas the body cannot do without. nitrogen is plentiful in air but does not keep cells alive.

q: Carbon dioxide is a gas given off as waste by animals and used as a raw material by ____.
e: Carbon dioxide is a gas given off as waste by animals and used as a raw material by plants. Animals give off carbon dioxide, and plants take that gas as a raw material for photosynthesis.

q: ____ gas is used as fuel.
e: Methane gas is used as fuel. Methane is the hydrocarbon gas burned as a fuel.

q: Ammonia gas which is a combination of nitrogen and hydrogen gases is used to make ____.
e: Ammonia gas which is a combination of nitrogen and hydrogen gases is used to make fertiliser. Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen and is the feedstock for nitrogen fertiliser. Ammonia is NH3, a combination of nitrogen with hydrogen.

q: Thus, it is important to study the behaviour of gases and their ____.
e: Thus, it is important to study the behaviour of gases and their reactions. Gas behaviour and gas reactions both matter because so much chemistry happens in the gas phase.

q: The volume and shape of all gases can be assumed as those of their ____.
e: The volume and shape of all gases can be assumed as those of their containers. A gas has no shape or volume of its own, so it takes the shape and volume of its container.

q: The intermolecular forces of gases are much ____ than those of other physical states.
e: The intermolecular forces of gases are much weaker than those of other physical states. Intermolecular forces in a gas are weak because the particles sit far apart compared with a liquid or solid.

q: Being the most ____ of the states of matter, they can be mixed evenly and completely when confined to the same container.
e: Being the most compressible of the states of matter, they can be mixed evenly and completely when confined to the same container. Gases are the most compressible state because most of the volume is empty space between particles.

q: Gases have much ____ densities than liquids and solids.
e: Gases have much lower densities than liquids and solids. Gas density is low because a small mass is spread through a large empty volume.

q: The ____ is a model that is used to predict gas behaviour.
e: The Kinetic Molecular Theory is a model that is used to predict gas behaviour. The kinetic molecular theory treats a gas as tiny particles in constant random motion with lots of empty space between them.

q: The volume of the particles themselves is ____ compared with the total volume of the gas.
e: The volume of the particles themselves is negligible compared with the total volume of the gas. The particles' own volume is negligible next to the volume of the gas, which is mostly empty space.

q: Most of the volume of the gas is ____ space.
e: Most of the volume of the gas is empty space. Most of a gas's volume is empty space, so the particles themselves take up a negligible share.

q: Gas molecules are in constant motion in ____ directions, and they frequently collide with one another.
e: Gas molecules are in constant motion in random directions, and they frequently collide with one another. Gas particles travel in random straight-line bursts and change direction only when they collide.

q: Collisions among molecules are perfectly ____.
e: Collisions among molecules are perfectly elastic. Elastic collisions keep the total kinetic energy of the particles. energy is not lost as heat in the ideal-gas picture.

q: In other words, energy can be ____ from one molecule to another as a result of a collision.
e: In other words, energy can be transferred from one molecule to another as a result of a collision. One mole is the amount that holds as many particles as 12 g of carbon-12, which is 6.02 x 10^23 particles. Energy can move from one molecule to another in a collision, while the total for the system stays the same.

q: the total energy of all the molecules in a system remains the ____.
e: The total energy of all the molecules in a system remains the same. Ideal-gas collisions are elastic, so the total kinetic energy of the molecules stays the same.

q: Gas molecules exert neither attractive nor ____ forces on one another.
e: Gas molecules exert neither attractive nor repulsive forces on one another. Ideal gas particles are treated as having no attractions or repulsions, only collisions.

q: The average kinetic energy of molecules is the same for all gases at the same ____.
e: The average kinetic energy of molecules is the same for all gases at the same temperature. Kelvin temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the gas particles.

q: its value is directly proportional to the ____ temperature.
e: Its value is directly proportional to the Kelvin temperature. Gas laws use Kelvin because that scale starts at absolute zero, where particle motion would stop.
